title: How Computers Count: Binary
summary: Computers use only two digits, 0 and 1. Learn to count and write numbers their way.

steps.title: Two digits only
sentences: Inside a computer there are billions of tiny switches that can be on or off.
We write 'on' as 1 and 'off' as 0, so computers use only two digits.
This way of writing numbers is called binary.

steps.title: Place values
sentences: In our normal numbers each place is worth ten times the one to its right.
In binary each place is worth two times the one to its right: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 and so on.
The binary number 101 means one four, no twos and one one, which is 5.

steps.title: Count to ten
sentences: So 1010 is ten, because it has one eight and one two.
Try finding your age in binary.

steps.title: From bits to everything
sentences: One binary digit is called a bit, and eight bits make a byte.
Letters, pictures, music and videos are all stored as long strings of bits.
The letter A, for example, is stored as the number 65, which is 01000001 in binary.

facts: A one-megabyte song file holds about eight million bits.
Computers are fast because switches can flip billions of times every second.
The idea of binary was written about by the Indian scholar Pingala around two thousand years ago and later by Gottfried Leibniz.
